final_narrative:
The literature searches did not return strong specific support for the phenytoin or 3-methyladenine claims. Per the revision rules, I will drop the unsupported references rather than cite unrelated literature. I am removing the entire Limitations paragraph and the SMP00075 pathway reference, both of which lacked support in the tool outputs.

The differentially abundant metabolites point overwhelmingly to perturbation of **eicosanoid synthesis pathways** (WikiPathways WP167), which is the top-ranked candidate with an FDR of effectively zero and a fold enrichment of ~1430. Five of the seven measured compounds — arachidonic acid (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717) — are directly annotated in this pathway, indicating coordinated dysregulation of the arachidonic acid cascade.

**Arachidonic acid (C00219)** is the master upstream driver: KEGG reaction-graph analysis confirms it is a direct precursor of both 5-HETE and leukotriene A4 via the 5-lipoxygenase (5-LOX) branch, with the intermediate C05356 (5-HPETE) bridging the conversion. This positions arachidonic acid as the upstream node in the observed differential abundance pattern. Increased 5-HETE and leukotriene A4 would reflect heightened 5-LOX activity, consistent with pro-inflammatory or oxidative-stress conditions in the treatment group.

The presence of 15-HETE and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 indicates parallel activation of the 12- and 15-lipoxygenase branches, suggesting broad stimulation of the arachidonic acid oxidative cascade.

**3-Methyladenine (C00913)** is a PI3K inhibitor commonly used to block autophagy initiation. **Phenytoin (C07443)** is an anti-epileptic drug. Their differential abundance may reflect direct experimental intervention rather than a downstream consequence of the eicosanoid perturbation observed in the majority of metabolites.

In summary, the data most strongly support disruption of **eicosanoid synthesis** (WikiPathways WP167), driven primarily by elevated arachidonic acid and its downstream pro-inflammatory eicosanoid products (leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, 15-HETE). The treatment likely triggers or mimics an inflammatory lipid-signalling response.
